topStories.headline: Early-Morning Fillmore Street Fire Displaces 19 Residents, Rescuers Pull 18 from Windows
topStories.dek: A 2-alarm blaze tore through a mixed-use building on the 800 block of Fillmore Street early Thursday, triggering a dramatic ladder rescue.
topStories.body:
San Francisco firefighters responded at approximately 1:56 a.m. Thursday, August 6, to a reported structure fire on the 800 block of Fillmore Street. First-arriving crews found a three-story, multi-residential building over commercial space with heavy fire showing, and quickly called a second alarm. Using ground and aerial ladders from multiple trucks, crews rescued 18 occupants stranded at second- and third-floor windows. One civilian was injured and is expected to recover.

The fire spread to a neighboring building at 855 Fillmore Street before being contained around 3:25 a.m. and declared under control at 3:33 a.m. A total of 19 residents from four units were displaced as a result of the blaze. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency provided a Muni bus as temporary shelter while the San Francisco Human Services Agency and the American Red Cross dispatched teams to assist.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation, and the total number of displaced residents is still being formally determined by city officials. The 900 block of Fillmore — the address also identified in some reports — sits within Supervisorial District 5, represented by Supervisor Bilal Mahmood. In July, Mahmood had already requested a public Board of Supervisors hearing to examine tenant oversight, safety conditions, and maintenance standards at multi-unit residential properties in the Western Addition.

Mayor Daniel Lurie thanked first responders in a social media post, noting that their quick action saved lives. The Board of Supervisors is currently in its annual summer legislative recess, which runs through August 28, meaning any formal city review of building safety tied to the incident would likely occur after the recess.

topStories.headline: SF Opera Unveils 2026–27 Season, Opening Night Set for September 12 at City Hall and War Memorial
topStories.dek: The company's 104th season launches with Verdi's Simon Boccanegra and a free Opera in the Park concert, as individual tickets go on sale now.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Opera has announced its 2026–27 season, led by Music Director Eun Sun Kim. The 104th season opens September 12 with Giuseppe Verdi's Simon Boccanegra — a new-to-the-company production — under Kim's baton, with the annual Opera Ball kicking off festivities at San Francisco City Hall and the War Memorial Opera House. The season runs through summer 2027 and concludes with Richard Wagner's Das Rheingold and Giacomo Puccini's Tosca.

Highlights include a new co-production with English National Opera of Thea Musgrave's Mary, Queen of Scots (September 20–October 4), and Das Rheingold, the prologue of Wagner's four-opera Ring cycle, in preparation for a full Ring mounting in 2028. Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro and Massenet's Manon round out the mainstage lineup. A free Opera in the Park concert returns to Robin Williams Meadow in Golden Gate Park on September 13, featuring Kim conducting the San Francisco Opera Orchestra and artists from the fall season.

The company will also continue its Dolby Tickets initiative, offering $10 tickets to eligible first-time Bay Area patrons, and will livestream the third performance of each mainstage production as part of its digital programming. Individual tickets went on sale July 7.

topStories.headline: Youth Urbanists Reimagine Downtown as DDC's Mid-Market Revival Gains Momentum
topStories.dek: High school students partnered with the San Francisco Downtown Development Corporation to propose bold new visions for Mid-Market, even as the DDC's $25M business fund begins dispersing grants.
topStories.body:
A summer program led by an urbanist youth nonprofit and the Downtown Development Corporation prompted San Francisco high schoolers to reimagine the downtown core, including proposals to replace the San Francisco Centre mall with housing and a public plaza. The SF Standard reported on the program July 28, highlighting student mockups that envision a more mixed-use, pedestrian-friendly Mid-Market corridor.

The exercise comes as the DDC's broader revitalization push enters a new phase. In April, the DDC and its partners launched a $25 million Downtown Business Fund designed to help businesses open and expand in San Francisco's downtown corridors, including Mid-Market. The fund offers grants up to $500,000 and loans from $100,000 to $1 million, with SF New Deal serving as an operating partner to assist small businesses in accessing resources.

The DDC, launched in 2025 under CEO Shola Olatoye, has already raised over $60 million in private, corporate, and philanthropic contributions from backers including Google, Ripple, Amazon, and Thoma Bravo. Its programs focus on five areas: clean and safe streets, business support, public spaces, arts and culture, and real estate. The effort is part of Mayor Daniel Lurie's broader downtown comeback strategy, which the SF Standard has described as the city's dominant recovery narrative heading into 2026.

moreNews.headline: SF Opera Season Tickets Available Now as 104th Season Approaches
moreNews.body: With the San Francisco Opera's 2026–27 season opening September 12, the company announced that individual tickets went on sale July 7 via sfopera.com or by calling (415) 864-3330. The season features six mainstage productions including the West Coast premiere of Thea Musgrave's Mary, Queen of Scots and Wagner's Das Rheingold. The company will also continue its Dolby Tickets program offering $10 seats to first-time Bay Area patrons.

moreNews.headline: Asian Art Museum Announces Landmark Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective Opening September 25
moreNews.body: The Asian Art Museum will present Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective, on view September 25, 2026 through January 25, 2027, marking the first major North American museum exhibition by the pioneering Korean contemporary artist. The show features more than 50 paintings tracing Ha's creative evolution over more than six decades, including two new works completed in 2025. The exhibition coincides with San Francisco's 50th anniversary of its sister city relationship with Seoul. Members can attend a preview and opening night on September 24.

moreNews.headline: Phoenix Hotel Lives On After Last-Minute Ownership Shift
moreNews.body: The iconic rock-and-roll Phoenix Hotel at 601 Eddy St. in the Tenderloin survived its reported New Year's closure after a last-minute change in operator. Despite announcing it would close January 1, 2026, the hotel's Instagram account rang in the new year with a statement that it was staying open. Mission Local reported in February that the property, purchased in 2024 by pastry chef Michel Suas, had new operators in place. The hotel's website continues to advertise summer poolside packages, keeping alive a cultural institution that has hosted everyone from David Bowie to Kurt Cobain.

moreNews.headline: Supervisor Mahmood Called for Tenant Safety Hearings Before This Week's Fillmore Fire
moreNews.body: Weeks before the August 6 Fillmore Street fire, District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood had already requested a public Board of Supervisors hearing to examine tenant oversight, safety conditions, and maintenance standards at multi-unit residential properties across the Western Addition, according to Mission Local. The hearing push followed tenant complaints at local housing developments. Any formal city review of the fire will have to wait until the Board's summer recess ends August 28, though special meetings can be called if needed.
